# IllegalArgumentException

<link-summary>An argument was of the wrong kind or outside the range the function accepts.</link-summary>

<web-summary>IllegalArgumentException — An argument was of the wrong kind or outside the range the function accepts. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>exception</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
class IllegalArgumentException extends RuntimeException
```

An argument was of the wrong kind or outside the range the function accepts. This is what most `requireX` guards throw.

Thrown by [`requireArray`](requireArray.md), [`requireInteger`](requireInteger.md), [`requireNonEmpty`](requireNonEmpty.md).

Every class in this hierarchy takes an optional message, another exception whose message it reuses, or nothing at all. `isException` recognises all of them; a plain `Error` is not one.

## Examples

### Throwing and catching

```javascript
throw new IllegalArgumentException("something specific about this call");

try {
  doWork();
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof IllegalArgumentException) {
    // handled
  }
}
```
